Subject: Initial questions on custody/escrow and retained backups (DPA)

Hi Stephanie / Marcus —

Thanks for walking Aurum Legal & SecOps through the DPA earlier today. We circulated the redline internally and have a few focused asks that our compliance team flagged — want to confirm we understand Redwood's posture before we propose edits. High-level items: 

- Escrow handover on acquisition: Aurum needs a mechanism for provisioned data handover to a designated buyer or trustee if Redwood is acquired; we prefer a technical handover (S3 snapshot + KMS transfer or custodian-held escrow).
- Purge triggers: clarify the timeline and mechanism for purging all customer data, including offsite backups and shards, after contract termination and after legal holds expire.
- Backup retention matrix: our auditors want a one-page matrix with timelines for hot cache, KV caches, daily backups, and long-term archives.
- Certification: we typically ask for a signed certificate of deletion within 30 days of purge for regionally-scoped data.

We attached the Aurum redline (Aurum_DPA_redline_v2.pdf) and a simple retention matrix for your reference. Can you confirm if Redwood can: (a) provide an escrow export format, (b) define purge SLAs for backups, and (c) issue a deletion certificate?

Appreciate a short call if helpful — ideally next week.

Best,
Alicia Rowe
Head of Legal Operations
Aurum

Subject: RE: Initial questions on custody/escrow and retained backups (DPA)

Alicia —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick responses and we can deep-dive on any specific line items: 

1) Escrow handover: Redwood can produce a custodial export package (encrypted bundle of customer blobs + metadata) for on-prem or third-party escrow. We do not transfer KMS keys directly; we provide a key-wrapped export and support a trustee process — engineer note: we can provide an S3-compatible export with MD5/SHA256 checksums.

2) Purge triggers & backups: Standard is:
   - Hot KV caches: purge immediate on termination (best-effort within 24 hours), ephemeral caches flushed immediately.
   - Daily backups: retained for up to 30 days by default unless contract specifies longer; we can shorten to 7/14/30 via SOW.
   - Long-term archives: retained per contract; if no retention term given, archives expire after 180 days and are scheduled for purge.

3) Certification: We can provide a deletion certificate for data in Redwood-managed systems within 30 days of completion of purge. For third-party backups (customer-managed or partner cloud), Redwood will provide attestation of actions taken but cannot certify partner processes beyond documented transfer steps.

I'll loop Marcus (runtime lead) and Naomi (security/compliance) to confirm the technical and evidence pieces. Priyom will weigh in on any commercial constraints.

If you want a single-page retention matrix from our side instead of the spreadsheet you sent, we can produce one by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Alicia —

Quick technical clarifications from the runtime side: 

- Export format: we will produce a gzipped manifest containing user blobs, model request logs (if requested in contract), and metadata JSON. We can support AES-256 key wrapping so Aurum's trustee can unwrap with a provided public key.
- KMS: Redwood uses a customer-specific KMS alias per Private deployment; for Hosted customers we manage keys by default. For any escrow transfer we will include a list of key aliases and provide the wrapped keys; we do not escrow plaintext keys.
- Backups in multi-region: for on-hosted customers we replicate snapshots to the region of record; purges will trigger deletion in the primary region and cascaded deletion in replicated regions within the same compliance window (we aim for 30 days for full propagation).

Note: we will need to carve out legal-hold exceptions that require manual confirmation before purge. That exception is operationally necessary and we'll capture steps in the playbook.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Alicia / team —

From procurement/legal side: two negotiation points we expect Aurum to consider if Redwood is to accept tighter SLAs/certifications: 

1) Fees for escrow exports & forensic support: detailed exports and KMS-related trustee support typically fall under professional services unless included in an enterprise plan. We can offer one complimentary escrow export per 12-month period; subsequent exports subject to a fixed fee (we propose $3,500/export).

2) Deletion certification scope: Redwood's deletion certificate will explicitly list systems covered (Redwood-managed runtime, primary backups, and snapshots). Partner-managed backups and customer-managed exports are out of scope. We can include an expanded certificate for customers on Dedicated or Private plans as part of the enterprise addendum.

If these commercial constructs are acceptable, we can reflect the fee and scope language in the next redline.

— Priyom
Principal, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — that is helpful and mostly aligns with our expectations. A few follow-ups before we finalize redlines: 

- Aurum accepts a trustee-wrapped-key approach (we prefer an industry escrow trustee; we will provide the public key during handover).
- We can accept the fee for additional exports; please include the $3,500 figure in the redline and call out one complimentary export in the first year.
- For deletion certificates: Aurum requests a statement of what was included (systems/list of S3 ARNs or bucket names) plus a signed representative name and timestamp.

If Redwood can produce the single-page retention matrix and an updated redline (with the export fee and the certificate scope), Legal will circulate for final sign-off. If agreeable, we can run DocuSign after redline confirmation — link below once you send over the revised DPA.
